chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Hadeed ibn Hakim who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man buys skins from the butcher, giving him a known amount every day.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a butcher a fixed daily amount in advance for skins?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility of *salam* (advance payment) contracts where the payment is made in installments rather than a lump sum, specifically validating a daily fixed amount for purchasing skins from a butcher. It highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding commercial credit arrangements, provided the quantity and quality of the goods are clearly defined to avoid *gharar* (uncertainty). This ruling supports practical trade mechanisms in early Islamic society by allowing deferred delivery against periodic prepayments.
